items.behavior: Solo mode pauses (never flushes) playback on speech onset while audible and then decides from the words. Since 2026-09-05 (D-032) REALTIME_SOLO_NAME_GATE defaults OFF: `_solo_interrupt_verdict` commits on a control phrase or any substantive transcript, and commits on sustained speech at REALTIME_BARGE_CONFIRM_MS=1600ms with no transcript at all. REALTIME_BARGE_MAX_PAUSE_MS=4000ms is gate-on-only code now (`=1` restores D-028's address rule). items.behavior: REALTIME_VAD_TYPE=semantic_vad with REALTIME_VAD_EAGERNESS=low (env already existed pre-round, D-003) is an alternative turn-detection mode to the default server_vad, intended to reduce fragment/backchannel commits at the cost of end-of-turn latency; semantic_vad reportedly misses 「對」/「好」 per the research doc. Since 2026-08-30 (D-028) this row ALSO covers the patience trial: eagerness sets a MAXIMUM wait (low ~8s, medium ~4s, high ~2s), not a fixed delay, so it is the better 'wait until I have finished' mechanism on paper — it is not documented as Mandarin-tuned, which is why the shipped default stayed server_vad with REALTIME_VAD_SILENCE_DURATION_MS raised 800 -> 1000. Under semantic_vad the server ignores that silence value entirely.
items.verification: On-robot A/B, same room and script: REALTIME_VAD_TYPE=server_vad + REALTIME_VAD_SILENCE_DURATION_MS=1000 (current default) vs. REALTIME_VAD_TYPE=semantic_vad + REALTIME_VAD_EAGERNESS=low. Measure (a) false-commit rate on backchannel utterances (嗯/對/好), (b) how often a deliberate ~1s Mandarin mid-sentence pause still cuts the speaker off, and (c) end-of-turn response latency, for each. Both directions matter: semantic_vad can win on patience and lose on backchannels.

items.behavior: A turn that proved itself an interruption only after the pause was over — rolled back by the REALTIME_BARGE_ROLLBACK_TIMEOUT_S timer, swallowed by the post-barge cooldown, or never armed — is still honoured: `_late_solo_interrupt` cancels the audible reply whatever its response id, flushes, truncates at the heard position and arms the repair watchdog so the turn cannot end in silence. Since 2026-09-05 (D-032) the late guard reads the SAME `_solo_interrupt_verdict` as the pause, so with the gate off a plain substantive sentence fires it (`late solo interrupt (substantive) on committed turn`), not only a name or 「停」. Eligibility is captured at speech onset and stamped per input item, so a turn that started in silence can never cancel its own answer and an out-of-order transcript cannot borrow another turn's onset. One exception: a reply the barge watchdog requested for this same utterance is never cancelled. Every declined turn now logs `late solo interrupt declined (audible=<bool>, verdict=<reason>)`.

(4) Watch for the duplicate-answer symptom: the answer plays, cuts within ~300 ms, and the same answer returns ~1.5 s later — that means the late path fired against the turn's own reply and the watchdog then repaired one that was never lost.

items.behavior: An interruption preserves the conversation instead of resetting it (operator requirement, 2026-09-05, D-032): `_cancel_active_response` stops the server generating, `_clear_queue` empties the local player, and `conversation.item.truncate` cuts the server's copy of every item that lost audio at `_heard_audio_ms()` (enqueued - outstanding - device buffer - 300ms slack, always rounded down). The model therefore keeps the words the user actually heard, drops the unheard tail, and answers the latest human speech rather than resuming where the old reply left off. Two items can be truncated in one barge: the paused one at its stashed position and the live one at a position measured before the flush. Best-effort: nothing is truncated when nothing was heard, and a server refusal is caught and now logged at INFO (`conversation.item.truncate refused`). Rollback paths never truncate — truncation is irreversible.
items.verification: On-robot in 一對一聊天模式 (plan T7 (d)): interrupt a long reply mid-sentence with a plain sentence, then ask 「你剛剛講到哪」. The answer must reference only the part that was actually spoken aloud before the cut, never the unheard remainder. Journal support on the same turn: a `conversation.item.truncate` goes out (no `conversation.item.truncate refused` line) and the follow-up answers the latest sentence rather than continuing the interrupted one.

items.behavior: Every COMMITTED interruption (solo commit, party barge, late interrupt) now sends conversation.item.truncate with the milliseconds actually heard — enqueued minus outstanding minus device buffer minus 300 ms slack, floored and always rounded DOWN. On WebSocket the server never trims an interrupted reply on its own, so without this the model believed it had spoken the whole reply and talked as if it had. Rollback paths never truncate (irreversible, and they resume the audio). Accepted biases (D-028): global outstanding under-counts, the pause path's device-buffer term can over-cut ~1.3 s, and a multi-item reply truncates only its last item — all in the safe direction.

items.behavior: Going to sleep leaves a callback behind: every person recognized during the app run gets ONE superseding `上次聊天（M月D日）：…` fact summarizing the visit. The visit is the unit — a bounded 40-item transcript tail (`session_transcript`) and the set of every name recognized this run (`recognized_people`) live on ToolDependencies and are deliberately NOT cleared on session reconnect, unlike `current_person`. Both are stamped with time.monotonic() (`recognized_at`, written only through `record_recognition`), because the two spans differ: once tail lines have been evicted, only people last seen at-or-after the oldest surviving line are summarized, so an all-day-awake robot cannot write tonight's topics into this morning's visitor's fact. Talking refreshes the speaker's stamp — current_person, or the SOLE guest when a reconnect has cleared that label (_run_realtime_session clears it on every session and the wake checks are one-shot per handler); with 2+ known and no label, nobody's — so a long visit, reconnects included, never summarizes nobody. Only the accepted user final and the assistant final are recorded (exactly two sites); the party-mode DENIED ambient turn and the solo-barge ROLLED-BACK backchannel are excluded — speech the robot decided was not addressed to it is not conversation. The summarizer runs once at handler shutdown, gated on `deps.sleep_requested` which ONLY the voice go_to_sleep closure sets (settings/backend restarts also reach shutdown() mid-visit), and it runs AFTER on_session_shutdown so the daemon's speaker is already stopped before a call that can take seconds. One gpt-5-mini call (MEMORY_LAST_CHAT_MODEL), MEMORY_LAST_CHAT_TIMEOUT_S 8.0 s clamped 1-30, MEMORY_LAST_CHAT_ENABLED kill switch; every failure logs an exception type and writes nothing. Supersession is by the 上次聊天 prefix alone (no PersonFact schema change): ADD then FORGET, with a FORGET-first branch at the 20-fact cap and whenever an old fact's forget-key is contained in the new one. Being newest-first the fact lands inside the FACE_GREETING_FACTS (6) facts the boot greeting and who_is_this already inject, so the next recognized boot can call back to it with no greeting-code change.

Session one: get recognized (boot or 「你認得我嗎」) and talk about something ongoing (an exam, a trip, a song being written), then say 「請進入睡眠模式」. The journal must show `Sleep summary: wrote last-chat fact for 1 person(s).` AFTER the music/session shutdown lines, and over ssh `people.v1.json` must hold exactly ONE fact for that person starting `上次聊天（` with today's date. Session two: boot recognized as the same person — the greeting must reference that thread (「上次你說…後來呢？」) rather than reciting facts, and `Startup greeting personalized for <name> with K remembered fact(s).` must show the callback among the K. Second negative control (visit window, needs the robot left awake): person A is recognized in the morning and talks; hours later, without any restart, person B is recognized and holds a long conversation (past the 40-line tail); on voice sleep the journal must report ONE person summarized and only B may gain a new 上次聊天 fact — A's must be untouched, still carrying its old date. Third session (supersession): repeat session one and confirm the person still has exactly ONE 上次聊天 fact, carrying the new date, with every real fact intact.
items.evidence: Unit-verified only (reachy_companion/tests/test_sleep_summary.py, 31 tests): the prefixed fact is written; a previous 上次聊天 fact is superseded; the same-day substring, case-variant and whitespace-variant collisions all leave exactly one fact — that trio was a PROVEN SILENT DELETE found in review, because forget_person_fact matches on a case-insensitive, whitespace-collapsed SUBSTRING newest-first, so guards keyed on raw text let the post-add forget remove the fact just written; at the 20-fact cap the forget-first branch keeps every real fact; no people or no transcript is a no-op; a client failure, bad JSON and an unlisted name all write nothing; the kill switch is honoured; the visit window is pinned four ways (2026-08-30) — a guest last seen hours before the retained tail is dropped and never even named to the model, one recognized mid-tail is kept, the sole speaker of a long visit is kept because talking refreshes the stamp, and an all-stale roster returns 0 with NO model call at all; the reconnect regression is pinned too — a websocket drop clears current_person and nothing re-sets it, so a single-guest visit that talks 50 more lines afterwards would have summarized NOBODY without the sole-guest fallback, while two known guests with no label refresh nobody; and the handler half is pinned twice — a shutdown WITHOUT sleep_requested writes nothing, and one WITH it summarizes exactly once with its own client and in the order ['music_stop', 'summary'], so the ordering cannot regress silently. BLOCKER: nothing here has run on the robot — this needs the SIXTEENTH INSTALL (the persona half is already live, sha 1ce532f3…, but every code path above rides the next wheel), and then a two-session live test with a real recognized person. RESIDUAL RISK to watch on that run: the summary is a network call inside shutdown, so a daemon that force-kills the app during sleep could race the <=8 s window and leave no fact — the failure is silent by design (no fact, no traceback), so judge it by the missing `Sleep summary:` journal line rather than by an error. SECOND RESIDUAL RISK, unmeasured: gpt-5-mini's real latency against MEMORY_LAST_CHAT_TIMEOUT_S=8.0 s — a reasoning model can spend that whole budget before its first token, and the timeout is a silent zero. Measure it on the FIRST on-robot run (journal time between the sleep lines and `Sleep summary:`); if it times out, raise the knob (clamped 1-30 s) or set the summarizer's reasoning effort low. THIRD RESIDUAL, deliberate: a guest is dropped once 40 transcript lines have elapsed since their last recognition or last heartbeat — WHETHER OR NOT they are still in the room speaking, because the heartbeat follows the current_person label (or the sole guest when a reconnect has cleared it) and there is no diarization; the case that loses a callback is a second guest in an unlabelled multi-person visit.

items.behavior: An operator-run pass tidies the Mac people store: companion_backend/scripts/consolidate.py hands each person's whole fact list to the model and stores back a merged, de-contradicted (「以前…，現在…」), usefulness-ranked one. Dry run by default and the printed unified diff IS the write — `after` is normalized and deduped exactly as store.replace_facts will hold it. An answer is validated whole or refused whole, and a refusal costs that person nothing. Writes go through store.replace_facts(..., preserve_updated_at=True), the store's only in-place writer, so a background pass never reshuffles the projection's recency ranking (position matters as much as the timestamp, because that sort is stable); the Mac store stays uncapped and only projection trims to 20. 上次聊天 facts are popped before the prompt, any the model invents is dropped, and only the newest is put back at position 0 — a keep-newest dedupe that HEALS the sync hole where robot-side removal detection is disabled at the 20-fact cap. Because the store lock is process-local, the CLI FAILS CLOSED: it first asks the kernel who holds the port (`lsof -nP -iTCP:8710 -sTCP:LISTEN`, which sees every bind including a LAN one no address list can guess), then probes :8710/api/config on loopback, COMPANION_BACKEND_HOST and the live `tailscale ip -4` (the documented production bind is the tailnet IP), and only a refused connection on every one of them lets the run continue; a missing lsof is not itself a refusal, because the probes are the floor. Exit codes 0 done / 1 refused or failed / 2 no OpenAI client / 3 backend up or unproven. --import-first and --push-after reuse backend/robot.py directly so the whole round trip runs with the backend stopped, in the only safe order; an empty store is never pushed.
